text: {"claims":[{"id":"c0","evidence":[{"sid":"P0.S0","rel":"entails"},{"sid":"P0.S1","rel":"entails"},{"sid":"P1.S2","rel":"entails"}],"check":null,"reasoning":"P0.S0 puts all database processes on one host; P0.S1 explains the shared-memory requirement; P1.S2 places the wal-index in that shared memory."},{"id":"c1","evidence":[{"sid":"P0.S0","rel":"entails"},{"sid":"P0.S1","rel":"entails"},{"sid":"P1.S4","rel":"entails"}],"check":null,"reasoning":"P0.S0 and P1.S4 state WAL cannot operate over a network filesystem, which covers the claim's NFS sharing case; P0.S1 explains separate hosts cannot share memory."},{"id":"c2","evidence":[{"sid":"P5.S1","rel":"refutes"},{"sid":"P5.S2","rel":"refutes"}],"check":null,"reasoning":"Same host alone is not sufficient: P5.S1 requires VFS shared-memory support for NORMAL first access, and P5.S2 says the open/convert attempt fails without it."},{"id":"c3","evidence":[{"sid":"P2.S2","rel":"entails"}],"check":null,"reasoning":"P2.S2 states the one-writer-at-a-time rule and attributes it to there being only one WAL file."},{"id":"c6","evidence":[{"sid":"P3.S0","rel":"entails"},{"sid":"P4.S0","rel":"entails"},{"sid":"P5.S0","rel":"entails"}],"check":null,"reasoning":"P3.S0 and P4.S0 allow no-shared-memory WAL when EXCLUSIVE is set before access; P5.S0 says NORMAL first creates the shared-memory wal-index, so avoiding it needs EXCLUSIVE first."},{"id":"c11","evidence":[{"sid":"P6.S2","rel":"refutes"}],"check":null,"reasoning":"P7.S1's no-block assurance is conditioned by P7.S0 on synchronous NORMAL; P6.S2 shows FULL makes writers sync every commit, so the unconditional guarantee is false."},{"id":"c12","evidence":[{"sid":"P6.S2","rel":"refutes"}],"check":null,"reasoning":"P6.S2 says synchronous FULL causes writers to sync on every commit, so the main/writer thread can block; the 'regardless' claim is false."}]}
